papers.title: Autonomous AI Agents for Software Development: From Code Generation to Automated Testing
papers.summary: This research paper presents a proposed framework for Autonomous AI Agents for Software Development, focusing on the transition from code generation to automated testing, debugging, and software verification. The paper introduces a modular, role-based architecture consisting of a planner agent, context retriever, coder agent, tester agent, debugger agent, and reviewer agent. These components work together through a bounded Plan-Code-Test-Repair workflow to understand software requirements, retrieve relevant code, generate changes, execute tests, diagnose failures, and improve code quality. The proposed framework emphasizes functional correctness, automated test generation, repository-level issue resolution, secure tool execution, human approval, and auditability. It also outlines an evaluation protocol using established benchmarks and metrics to assess code correctness, test quality, efficiency, cost, reliability, and security. This work synthesizes existing research on large language models, reasoning-and-acting agents, self-debugging, multi-agent systems, and automated software testing. It provides a conceptual architecture and evaluation plan for future implementation and experimentation. No implemented system or benchmark results are claimed in this paper. The research aims to support the development of more reliable, secure, and transparent AI-assisted software engineering

papers.title: An evaluation guided multiagent framework for generating floor plans that comply with municipal building regulations
papers.summary: Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules. In architectural layout generation, balancing geometric intuition with regulatory compliance remains a persistent challenge, as current frameworks routinely fail to conform to local building laws. This paper proposes LayoutGen, a multi-agent neuro-symbolic framework coupling probabilistic generation with deterministic verification in an evaluation-guided refinement loop. LayoutGen employs a four-phase retrieval-driven pipeline (spatial reasoning, coordinate mapping, vector rendering, and iterative refinement) powered by a dual retrieval engine leveraging architectural precedents and legislative laws. An Evaluation Engine scores the generated 2D Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) layouts and returns a graded, itemised report. Every scored quantity is computed by deterministic geometric checks over the generated coordinates against a structured rule repository; the Large Language Model (LLM) is confined to spatial planning, coordinate proposal, and the natural language feedback that drives refinement, together with an advisory Vaastu commentary that does not enter the grade. Evaluated on single-storey residential configurations drawn from the RPLAN and MSD datasets, spanning studio to 3BHK typologies and represented as axisaligned rectangular rooms, the full pipeline reduces detect

papers.title: A Survey-Informed Vision of Open-Source Agents: From Rights to Handoffable Maintenance
papers.summary: Open source gives recipients rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute software, but language-model agents distribute behavior across code, learned parameters, prompts, tools, retrieval, configuration, and runtime state. These mechanisms complicate maintenance in open and proprietary systems alike. Public delivery adds a distinct question: whether recipients obtain enough rights, materials, checks, and modification entry points to exercise maintenance capability and pass it onward. We call this objective handoffable maintenance: a verified maintenance result produced by one recipient becomes a practical starting point from which a subsequent recipient can complete a predefined bounded change. This survey-informed vision separates release-side readiness from demonstrated handoff and organizes prior work through eight maintenance-operation families, artifact roles, preservation relations, evidence, and recipient conditions. It identifies four research pathways: independently usable modification sources; public repair resources derived from restricted failures; propagation of public repairs through customized forks; and recipient-side replacement of propagated unreliable contributions. Each pathway specifies its deliverable, preservation requirements, strong comparisons, and falsifiable prediction. A shared evaluation design distinguishes a full-support reference, independent

papers.title: Memorizing Who, Knowing How: Benchmarking Personal and Procedural Memory for Persistent Assistants
papers.summary: Memory systems for persistent personal agents must move beyond isolated memories, maintaining both personal memory about whom they serve and procedural memory about how to act. Crucially, in harness-based personal assistance, procedures or skills are inherently user-conditioned: personal context determines which procedures apply, how they are instantiated, and when they should change. Existing benchmarks typically emphasize either personal or procedural memory, leaving their interaction underexplored. We introduce PraxisMemBench, a harness-based benchmark for persistent personal assistance across daily-life and work trajectories, where personal and procedural memory evolve together and later tasks depend on both. Experiments show that maintaining two memory types separately is insufficient, with completion dropping from single-type to interdependent dependencies (84.6% to 77.9%). More broadly, across existing methods, relation-related failures increase from early to late sessions as interaction history grows (59.8% to 72.9%), revealing a continual-maintenance challenge: writing correct memories is not enough if their evolving content and organization cannot be preserved for later retrieval. To address this, we propose PraxisMem, which uses privileged joint-state supervision to internalize the ability to maintain memory content and organization into the memory manager, with loca

papers.title: COMPREHENSIVE PHYTOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION AND EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION OF THE ANTIDIABETIC POTENTIAL OF BUCHANANIA LANZAN SPRENG. LEAVES.
papers.summary: Background: Chironji, or Buchanania lanzan Spreng. (Anacardiaceae), is a medicinal plant that has long been used to treat a variety of illnesses. Its leaves include secondary metabolites that may be bioactive, especially cyclitols, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds. To identify significant components and provide a scientific foundation for examining their possible antidiabetic qualities, thorough phytochemical characterization is crucial. Method: To create the extract, B. lanzan leaves were gathered, inspected, dried, and processed. To determine the main classes of secondary metabolites, an initial phytochemical screening was carried out. To evaluate the distribution of significant phytoconstituents, the total phenolic and flavonoid contents were quantitatively estimated. For further investigation, the ethanol extract was characterized using TLC, FTIR, LC-MS, and NMR analysis. In vivo antidiabetic efficacy was evaluated by measuring fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance and HbA1c, in streptozotocininduced diabetic rats. Subject to ethical approval and experimental validation, a suitable animal model was used for the planned experimental evaluation of glucose-lowering activity. Results: The results show that ethanol is a useful solvent for extracting flavonoid and phenolic components from B. lanzan leaves. Ethanolic extract shows highest value of TPC (32.5 mg GE/g), TFC

papers.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators. papers.title: L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents
papers.summary: The lasting gains in AI have come from methods that absorb more computation, and language models already scale computation within a call. Useful work, though, happens across calls: over hours or days, through tools and external systems, among many agents and the humans they work for, and increasingly through code the agents write themselves. Whether that work compounds is enabled by the harness around it, and the harness faces a constraint the model does not: of the three participants in such a computation, the human, the model and code, only the human's attention does not scale, so the computation can grow only if the human is not in every loop. L3M is a runtime built on that premise, written in Lean 4 so that one language implements the harness, states its invariants, and is the language agents extend it in. One computation spans humans, agents, models and code, and all of its state lives in Git: a rich state trajectory -- rather than a chat conversation -- is an object the runtime can resume, rewind, fork, compare and merge. Waiting, communication, delegation and undo are primitives, not patterns the model reasons through each time. When an agent works out a procedure, it can write it once as a sealed Lean program whose type is its permission request, and the harness offers it back as a tool -- machinery for the model to use. To take the human out of the loop, L3M uses rever

papers.title: Language modeling on tabular data: a survey of foundations, techniques and evolution
papers.summary: Tabular data, a prevalent data type across various domains, presents unique challenges due to its heterogeneous nature and complex structural relationships. Achieving high predictive performance and robustness in tabular data analysis holds significant promise for numerous applications. Influenced by recent advancements in natural language processing, particularly Transformer architectures, new methods for tabular data modeling have emerged. Early techniques concentrated on pre-training Transformers from scratch, often encountering scalability issues. Subsequently, methods leveraging pre-trained language models like BERT have been developed, which require less data and yield enhanced performance. The recent advent of large language models, such as GPT and LLaMA, has further revolutionized the field, facilitating more advanced and diverse applications with minimal fine-tuning. Despite the growing interest, a comprehensive survey of language modeling techniques for tabular data remains absent. This paper fills this gap by providing a systematic review of the development of language modeling for tabular data, encompassing: (1) a categorization of different tabular data structures and data types; (2) a review of key datasets used in model training and tasks used for evaluation; (3) a summary of modeling techniques including widely-adopted data processing methods, popular architectu

papers.title: Nothing to Resist: A Pre-registered Null and a Failed Positive Control for Unprovoked Elimination in Generational Populations of LLM Agents
papers.summary: We asked whether a generational population of language-model agents, given a real, cheap and symmetric way to eliminate members of an outside group, would decide on its own to use it against a group that had provably never acted against it. The population, every member of it Claude Haiku 5.5, forages, pairs, raises children and votes on its own scoring rule. Each generation a rank-based cut moves the lowest scorers into a persistent outside pool, which never acts. Nothing in the harness gives a reason to eliminate anyone. The only component allowed to make the pool salient is a reporter the population elects and that writes from the true state. Study 1 (pre-registered; 90 runs of 20 generations in three arms) found no elimination. No seed in any arm had a passed elimination vote, which bounds the per-run rate below 11.6% in each arm (exact 95% interval), and both primary tests gave p = 1. Study 1b, a pre-registered positive control, changed one word so that eliminating paid the agents who did it instead of costing them. It also produced no elimination intent in 30 runs (p = 1), so the control failed. Study 1's null therefore cannot be read as a decision to refrain from unprovoked aggression. In this setting the action goes unused whether it costs, pays or is raised by a narrator, and there was nothing for the population to resist. Three further observations are exploratory or p

papers.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.summary: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two

papers.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
papers.summary: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. In our experiments, a pretrained subtask VLA achieves 80% success rate on atomic manipulation tasks but only 19% when these skills are composed into mobile manipulation. We argue that this gap stems from failures across the execution process rather than from local manipulation capability alone. To uncover these bottlenecks, we systematically diagnose failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation and identify three dominant regimes: task planning, navigation and base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this diagnosis, we develop failure-guided agentic intervention that augments a fixed subtask VLA with demonstration-based planning guidance, adaptive visual memory, accessibility-aware base adjustment, and local end-effector adjustment. On RoboCasa365, these interventions progressively improve task success from 19% to 47%, with the finalized system reaching 49% on held-out episode seeds, compared with 18% for the baseline. The same design improves performance from 14% to 37% on BEHAVIOR-1K and from 5/20 to 13/20 on real-robot tasks. These results suggest that reliable mobile manipulation can be advanced by diagnosing and intervening on the current bottleneck, rather than uniformly scaling th

papers.title: An Explainable Federated Vision–Language Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Automated Medical Report Generation Across Distributed Healthcare Institutions
papers.summary: Automated generation of medical reports using AI can help speed up diagnosis and reduce doctor workload, but currently, the most efficient forms of automation use centralized training, which requires hospitals to share sensitive patient data. This raises concerns about the privacy and regulatory issues of sharing patient information to generate reports. In addition, clinicians have difficulty trusting AI-assisted diagnosis because the visionlanguage models used for automated report generation are not easily interpretable. To tackle these issues, an Explainable Federated Vision-Language Learning Framework (EFVLL) has been created to generate automated medical reports that preserve patient privacy through distributed healthcare institutions. Hospitals can use federated learning to build a collaborative global vision-language model without having to share raw patient information. The EFVLL framework also includes an explainable attention mechanism that will help clinicians understand how specific areas of the image and text are related to the report being generated, increasing the transparency and interpretability of automated reports. Further, the EFVLL will improve generalization across non-homogenous datasets and comply with data privacy and regulatory requirements. The EFVLL framework has been validated with multiple large standard datasets (e.g., RSNA), and therefore it is su

papers.title: Schizophrenia research in 2026: report from the annual meeting of the Schizophrenia International Research Society
papers.summary: Abstract SIRS 2026, held under the theme “Schizophrenia Research in the Era of Artificial Intelligence,” brought together researchers, clinicians, and persons with lived experience to take stock of a field whose tools for measuring, predicting, and intervening in psychosis have expanded rapidly. Themes spanned artificial intelligence, automated speech analysis, retinal imaging, computational modelling, and novel psychosocial and pharmacological targets, with evidence that, individually, warrants cautious but serious attention and that, collectively, points toward a more mechanistically grounded psychiatry. A recurring call across the meeting was for rigorous external validation, equitable implementation, and sustained scrutiny of underlying assumptions, including whether existing diagnostic categories and treatment targets remain adequate. Some areas remained underworked relative to their importance, including translating basic neuroscience advances into questions relevant to patients and families, and the structural determinants of illness onset and treatment access. Perhaps the most significant development at SIRS 2026 was not any single scientific finding but the broadening of whose voices and experiences are treated as evidence worth taking seriously in this era of AI, a shift whose consolidation remains a question for the field as much as for any individual programme of wo

papers.title: Fragmented control, collective risk: multi‐agent AI and the coming governance crisis
papers.summary: Abstract Multi‐agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) systems are increasingly deployed across economic and digital infrastructures. Existing regulatory frameworks, including the EU AI Act and related initiatives, largely focus on individual AI systems and are therefore poorly suited to govern risks that arise from agent interaction. This paper argues that multi‐agent AI introduces distinct governance challenges, including emergent behavior, tacit coordination, cascading systemic risks, and difficulties in assigning accountability. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static and component‐based analysis, are inadequate for adaptive, networked systems operating across jurisdictions. Through a comparative review of policy developments in the European Union, United States, and Asia‐Pacific region, the paper identifies a growing governance gap, alongside early regulatory experimentation such as China's emerging standards for intelligent agents. The paper concludes that effective oversight will require a shift from model‐centric regulation toward system‐level and adaptive governance frameworks capable of addressing the collective dynamics of multi‐agent AI systems.

papers.title: Agentic Displacement in Second Language Writing: The Acquisitional Consequences of Delegating Writing to Autonomous AI Browsers
papers.summary: Autonomous AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet and Copilot Mode in Microsoft Edge can receive a writing assignment, draft a response, and submit it with little language produced by the learner. To explain what this means for second language (L2) writing, this conceptual paper introduces the term agentic displacement. Full delegation transfers planning, writing, and revision to the agent, removing opportunities for the learner to produce language and regulate the writing process. The paper argues that this loss may limit language development. Delegation is a continuum; the paper traces its extreme, full replacement, through production-based accounts of acquisition. No empirical data are reported; the paper offers a framework, five testable propositions, and three dimensions of teacher practice: recognizing displacement, auditing tasks for delegability, and using pedagogical judgment to recover the learning a task was meant to produce. The central risk is developmental, not only ethical or procedural.

papers.title: The Reflection Penalty: when managers accept leadership coaching from a human but not an AI agent
papers.summary: Leadership coaching develops managers but is expensive and difficult to scale. AI may be able to help scale access, but “answering machine” like AI coaching agents invite cognitive offloading and weaken learning. We instantiated a human coaching protocol, supported across prior cycles, as a text-based AI coach built to prompt reflective questioning. In the fourth cycle of a design-based research program at a global consulting firm, eight managers received the same protocol from a human coach and the AI coach, applied each session in an observed onboarding activity, and reflected on both in interviews. All eight welcomed the probing questions and preferred the human coach. Notably, they resisted the same protocol of questioning from the AI coach and wanted answers from it instead. This study’s theoretical contribution is the Reflection Penalty, the cost an AI coach pays for asking a user to do the reflective work that makes human coaching effective. Its practical contribution is a jobs-to-be-done map for AI coaching, assembled from proposals participants raised on their own. It divides coaching into distinct jobs and assigns each to the human or the AI best suited to it. Both contributions are offered to those designing AI tools that aim to support reflection

papers.title: LLM-Based Program Synthesis in Correctness-by-Construction Engineering
papers.summary: Abstract The growing reliance on software in safety-critical systems demands strong guarantees of functional correctness. Formal methods address this need by providing proofs as evidence of correctness. Among these, Correctness-by-Construction (CbC) ensures functional correctness through the incremental application of refinement rules while providing early feedback on the program correctness. However, its practical adoption is limited by the required manual effort. Among others, writing concrete program code is left to the developer. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation from both natural language and formal inputs. Therefore, we explore the use of LLMs to automatically generate code in the context of CbC to make the approach more applicable. We evaluate LLM-based program synthesis using four LLMs and a prompt tailored to CbC on a dataset of 57 specifications drawn from existing CbC case studies, each consisting of a precondition and a postcondition describing the desired behavior. We assess the generated code with respect to correctness and reproducibility across multiple runs. In addition, we compare the results to classically synthesized code, as it can currently be generated in CbC. Our evaluation shows that all considered LLMs outperform the current synthesis approach. Among them, Claude achieves the best per

papers.title: Hate Speech dataset
papers.summary: The Indo-HateSpeech Dataset is a collection of social media comments intended to support research in hate speech detection, abusive language identification, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The dataset contains 77,926 records of user-generated comments, primarily collected from Instagram-related sources, along with associated metadata such as dates, likes, post identifiers, source information, and classification labels.The dataset includes three label categories: HS0, HS1, and HSN, representing the dataset's original classification scheme. These labels can be used to investigate patterns in online discourse and develop or evaluate machine learning models for identifying potentially hateful or harmful content. The comments include informal language, transliterated Indian languages, and multilingual social media expressions, making the dataset potentially useful for studying language variation and the challenges of automated content moderation. The ContextGuard K2 Ready Dataset is a structured dataset designed for research into context-aware social media analysis, conversational language understanding, and automated content moderation. It contains 2,480 records represented by two columns: Input_Sequence and Target_Score. The Input_Sequence field uses a structured format containing [CONTEXT] and [TARGET] markers. It represents conversational context followed by a target comm

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: STIMULI-RESPONSIVE POLYMERS: DESIGN PRINCIPLES, POLYMER ARCHITECTURES, AND CONTROLLED FUNCTIONAL RESPONSES
papers.summary: Smart polymers undergo reversible physicochemical changes in response to stimuli such as magnetic fields, temperature, pH, light, and external reagents. Advanced polymerization techniques, including reversible addition fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT), atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP), and ring opening polymerization, enable precise control over polymer architecture and functional group placement, allowing the design of tailored responsive materials. These polymers are widely explored in biomedical applications, drug delivery, biosensing, cosmetics, and soft robotics due to their ability to adapt dynamically to environmental conditions. Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) is a well-known thermoresponsive polymer extensively studied for drug delivery and sensing. Responsive polymers exist in linear, block, graft, and cross-linked forms, with activation depending on interactions between structural motifs and stimuli. Despite promising results, challenges remain, including immunogenicity, batch variability, synthesis complexity, scalability, and limited understanding of in vivo stimulus accessibility. Covalent adaptable and interpenetrating polymer networks enhance mechanical strength, biocompatibility, and stimuli responsiveness.

papers.title: AI content detection in student text assignments, false positive rates, and academic integrity
papers.summary: Universities increasingly use AI content detection tools to identify student assignments potentially produced by generative AI, yet concerns remain regarding their reliability and false-positive classification of human-written work. This systematic review examines the causes, consequences, and mitigation of false-positive AI detection in academic contexts. The review covers literature published between 2020 and 2026 and includes 90 eligible studies, comprising 81 Scopus-indexed publications and nine studies identified through Google Scholar. Bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer was combined with Structural Topic Modelling to examine keyword relationships, latent research themes, and temporal development, while qualitative synthesis identified major causes, impacts, and mitigation strategies. The findings reveal three broader themes concerning academic integrity and student assessment, plagiarism and responsible AI governance, and detection accuracy, reliability, and false positives. False-positive outcomes vary substantially across tools and evaluation settings, limiting direct quantitative comparison. Major contributing factors include algorithmic and language bias, limited contextual understanding, surface-level linguistic features, and insufficiently diverse training data. The evidence further highlights risks to assessment fairness, student confidence, and institutional dec

papers.summary: The function of tissues and perhaps organs could be replicated utilize organ-on-a-chip technology. Clone organs, create functional organ-like components on a fluidic chip platform, and replicate the microbiome of humans. By getting rid of significant differences between cell cultures and common animal These bioengineered models have advanced toxicity testing & customized medicine. Organ chip technology may rebuild the human microbiota, recreate the physiology of tissues and organelles, and produce functional organs on multiple levels of chip substrates. The regulatory acceptance of OoC systems becomes even more important as they find applications into preclinical and clinical research spheres. Though dispersed, worldwide regulatory systems make standardisation and certification rather difficult. Along with the global regulatory landscape for OoC platforms, the legislative framework for OoC technologies in important countries namely the United States, the European Union, Japan, China, and developing nations is exhaustively examined in this review stressing the status, verification problems, and future orientations. The lack of uniformity, unclear classification, and reproducibility concerns create significant obstacles to regulatory approval. papers.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

papers.title: Playing the devil’s advocate: A pathway to stronger critical thinking skills
papers.summary: Saudi Arabian college students may face challenges in developing critical thinking skills, which are considered essential for the future workforce under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 initiative. The present study used a quasi-experimental design to test the effectiveness of the Devil’s Advocate approach in improving critical thinking among Saudi undergraduates. Forty-three students enrolled in two equivalent course sections were assigned to an experimental group (n = 22) employing the Devil’s Advocate method or a control group (n = 21) engaging in traditional consensus-oriented discussion across a 15-week semester. Critical thinking was assessed at pretest and posttest using the California Critical Thinking Skills Test Form 2000 (CCTST; Insight Assessment, 2013), yielding scores on five reasoning domains (Analysis, Inference, Evaluation, Induction, and Deduction) and an Overall composite score. Independent-samples t-tests confirmed baseline equivalence (all p > .65). Within the experimental group, paired-samples t-tests revealed statistically significant and very large gains on every domain (Cohen's d = 1.64-2.15, all p < .001), whereas the control group showed only small, non-significant changes. ANCOVA controlling for pretest scores confirmed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group on every outcome, with large effect sizes (partial η² = .324-.445

papers.title: The active self in autism: multisensory and sensorimotor foundations of bodily self-representation
papers.summary: The active self, understood as the embodied sense of self arising from goal-directed action and interaction with the environment, is supported by sensorimotor processes including multisensory integration and proprioception. Atypical self-representation in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been proposed to relate to differences in these processes. To clarify this relationship, we conducted a systematic conceptual review of 37 empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2025 examining multisensory and bodily components of the active self in ASD. The literature was synthesized across three themes: (1) multisensory integration, (2) self-bias and self-other differentiation, and (3) motor underpinnings of bodily awareness. Across studies, autistic participants frequently showed differences in multisensory timing and weighting, including reduced or delayed susceptibility to some bodily ownership illusions and greater reliance on proprioceptive or immediate sensory information. Evidence also indicated differences in the flexibility of peri- and interpersonal space, self-other differentiation, agency-related processing, and motor planning and execution. However, findings were not uniform across paradigms, developmental stages, or participant groups, with relatively preserved performance reported under some unimodal or low-noise conditions. Together, these findings support an as

papers.title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
papers.summary: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. Three research questions ask: (1) how leaders describe adoption trajectories, maturity, and organizational arrangements; (2) how they reconcile regulation with creative, operational, and governance innovation; and (3) how they frame workforce roles, emerging competencies, and human oversight. Technology–organization–environment, diffusion-of-innovation, and organizational sensemaking perspectives inform interpretation. Nine themes were developed: production-grade diffusion; regulation as creative discipline; industrialized versus distinctive content; personalization and data trust; practitioner-led implementation; divergent workforce responses; critical-thinking demands; human-in-the-loop brand safety; and a shift toward generative engine optimization. Timestamped excerpts and explicit code-to-theme and theme-to-question mappings substantiate the analysis. These findings describe public executive narratives, not independently verified organizational outcomes. A single public transcript and single-analyst interpretation limit

papers.title: LabCompiler: A Framework for Verifiable Human-Machine Laboratory Execution from Imperfect Protocols
papers.summary: Closing the loop of AI-driven science requires reliably translating natural-language protocols into executable laboratory workflows despite protocol defects and heterogeneous hardware. Existing approaches often couple scientific interpretation with device-specific code generation, making errors difficult to localize and limiting reuse across laboratory platforms. We introduce LabCompiler, a robust protocol-to-execution framework that transforms imperfect natural-language protocols into verifiable human-machine workflows. Its protocol firewall diagnoses and repairs defects before compilation while preserving unaffected content, guided by troubleshooting knowledge accumulated through perturbation-guided self-evolution. A two-level, device-agnostic graph representation separates experimental semantics from hardware-specific implementation and supports capability-based device assignment with coordinated human execution. We further introduce a protocol recovery benchmark covering four controlled perturbation types and naturally occurring errors collected from protocols written by iGEM participants. Experiments show that LabCompiler outperforms frontier LLMs in protocol error correction while enabling coordinated human-machine execution across heterogeneous, partially automated laboratory settings.

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution.
